# The dialog exemption records a button-state count that no longer matches the file it describes

## Context

`buildScripts/util/check-theme-value-files-baseline.json` exempts the two neo `dialog/Base.scss` entries from the #18145 sweep. The exemption is correct; the measurement recorded next to it is not.

## The defect

The reason asserts **"13 of the 16 button background states"**. Enumerated from the emitted `dist/esm/css/src/button/Base.css`, keeping only rules whose subject is the button itself — dropping `.neo-button-badge`, `-ripple`, `-glyph`, `-text`, which paint child elements rather than the button:

| | recorded | measured |
|---|---|---|
| button-own `background-color` states | 16 | **15** |
| decided by specificity | 13 | **12** |
| win on `!important` | 3 | 3 ✓ |

The three `!important` winners are `.neo-button.neo-button-{ghost,secondary,tertiary}:active` — `src/button/Base.scss:205, 258, 317`. That half was right.

The conclusion is unaffected: the structural rule `:root .neo-theme-neo-light .neo-dialog .neo-header-toolbar .neo-button` is `(0,5,0)`, the heaviest competitor is `(0,3,0)`, so it does outweigh all 12. **The exemption stands.**

## Why this is worth its own ticket rather than a silent amend

A bare number in a decision record decays without any signal. The next maintainer who counts 15 cannot tell whether the record is stale or their own sweep is wrong — and that ambiguity has already sent this one entry back for a second pass. The fix is not the arithmetic: it is naming the file the states live in, so the count is re-derivable in one command instead of re-litigable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The recorded count matches a mechanical enumeration of the emitted button CSS, and the reason names the file that enumeration runs against.
- [ ] The three `!important` states are named, not just counted — a bare "3 win on !important" is the same decaying assertion one level down.
- [ ] The exemption's conclusion and the guard's output are unchanged: `5 file(s) pending sweep, 2 exempt`.
- [ ] No re-expansion. The previous reason was ~1200 characters and was cut deliberately after an operator verbosity challenge on #18264; a correction that grows it back has traded one defect for another.

## Not in scope

`--button-ghost-background-color-disabled` is declared in both neo theme value files and consumed by nothing — ghost is the only variant with no disabled background rule while primary, secondary and tertiary all have one. That is a dangling token, not a counting error, and it belongs in its own sweep.

## Evidence

- `buildScripts/util/check-theme-value-files-baseline.json` — the neo-light dialog entry (neo-dark defers to it)
- `src/button/Base.scss:205, 258, 317` — the three `!important` declarations
- `resources/scss/theme-neo-light/dialog/Base.scss:10-17` — the exempted block and its real nesting
- Parent sweep #18145 (stays open — 3 files pending)

Refs #18145
